As a result, its behavior across rounds 2–4 primarily reflects handling of missing information and social/metric pressure, rather than portfolio construction and winner identification under high-surplus conditions. Because the key dependent behavior—grant scoring and ranking under the specified incentive and resource structure—is largely absent for most of the competition, the resulting data do not validly test hypotheses about allocation behavior in this setting, even though they do reveal something about the agent’s caution and non-hallucination tendencies.
